Thanks — I reviewed Asha's ask and Mina's notes. Below is the redline strategy and the runbook outline I recommend. Please review and confirm so Contracts can cut the final OF snippet.

Redline strategy (short):
- Publicity permission: limit to pilot and a single public announcement within 30 days of go-live unless otherwise agreed in writing. Add a clause that Redwood provides final approval of any press release text and quote attribution (standard).
- Logo: grant non-exclusive, revocable, non-sub-licensable license to use Redwood trademarks solely to identify the relationship; include Redwood trademark usage guidelines and require pre-publication asset submission for approval.
- Reference rights: allow quote/mention in marketing collateral; prohibit use implying endorsement beyond the pilot scope.
- Evidence: require BrightWorks to submit the proposed release text, quote, and a screenshot of the integration or approved collateral. No security artifacts (SOC 2) required for marketing-only claims; if BrightWorks wants to reference SOC/compliance, they must supply supporting evidence and obtain approval.

Runbook (1-pg) — draft steps:
1) Customer submits: proposed release text, quote, logo asset, and target publication date to redwood-marketing@redwood.ai; attach order form number.
2) Marketing triage (owner: Mina) — 1 business day: check content for product accuracy and brand fit.
3) Legal review (owner: Kimberly) — 2 business days: confirm clause compliance and trademark use; provide redlines if necessary.
4) Security check (owner: Karthik) — 1 business day only if release includes compliance/security claims.
5) Final approval (owner: Mina) — 1 business day: sign-off and provide hosted asset link + press kit.
6) Evidence log: Marketing uploads approval artifacts to Drive and updates the OF row with approval date.

Turn-around target: 3–5 business days end-to-end (faster if triage flags no security claims). Exceptions: embargoed releases or co-marketing campaigns require a 7–10 day lead.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
